newsitem.title: INDIA: India ICICI, Prudential in tie up.
newsitem.headline: India ICICI, Prudential in tie up.

text.p: Term lender Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India (ICICI) has tied up with Prudential Corp, Britain's largest insurance firm, to enter the life insurance sector once it opens up, officials said.

"We have today signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the intent to get into the life insurance business in anticipation of the government opening up this sector," ICICI Managing Director K.V. Kamath told a news conference.
The MoU envisages that the two will jointly explore opportunities in the life insurance business, the firms said in a joint statement.

"The two institutions also agreed to examine the areas of healthcare, pensions and mutual funds with the goal of eventually providing a full range of life insurance and other financial products," the statement added.
ICICI and Prudential will be equal partners in the venture, Kamath said. ICICI is relying on Prudential's skills in technology and marketing to help it master the life insurance business, he added.
"The next step is to await the opening up of the sector," he said. "In the medium term we are sure it will be opened up, but in the meantime there is a lot to be done."

"We'll wait as long as necessary," Mark Tucker, Managing Director of Prudential Corp Asia, said, when asked how long Prudential was willing to wait for the Indian insurance sector to be opened up. "I've been waiting ten years for a license in China and am still waiting."

The partners have no immediate plans to tap the health insurance sector, which former Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said should be thrown open in his 1997/98 budget proposals, to be debated in parliament next week.

ICICI is also looking for a partner to enter the non-life sector. Prudential has sought clearance for a holding company, Prudential Corp India Pvt Ltd, through which it will route its investments into India.

Prudential is one of Britain's biggest institutional investors, with over $ 145 billion worldwide. It recently launched its Prudential Invest Direct Asia targeted at making direct investments in China, Indian and Vietnam.
ICICI's main business focus is project and corporate financing, with 4,900 companies and 13,200 projects financed by September 30,1996, aggregating fund deployment of 413 billion rupees.
